title: Rabbi Yehuda ben Pappus
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A great man in the time of Rabban Gamliel, as in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:9: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua were walking along the road and turning aside to its edges. They saw Rabbi Yehudah ben Pappus sinking into the road as he came toward them. Rabban Gamliel asked Rabbi Yehoshua, “Who is this who points himself out with a finger?” He replied, “It is Yehudah ben Pappus, all of whose deeds are for the sake of Heaven.” Bava Kamma 81b relates a similar incident concerning Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] and Yehudah ben Nekusa. Hyman suggests that “he” may have been the father of Pappus ben Yehudah, Rabbi Akiva’s colleague, as in Berakhot 61b.

notes.text: In the saved Guggenheimer edition of Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:9, the full paragraph permits travellers to turn to the road’s edges because of obstacles, even into planted fields when sinking. Yehudah ben Pappus instead approaches while sinking into the road. This context supports the road-related sense of משתקע. Hyman’s conjecture about Pappus’s father still has an ambiguous referent: the subject of this notice or Yehudah ben Nekusa. Bava Kamma פא: is 81b under the supplied colon convention.

The whole Guggenheimer Berakhot 2:9 paragraph directly names the three walkers and supplies the road-obstacle/sinking context. The ambiguous father conjecture and the different Bava Kamma names remain Hyman’s discussion; a similar incident does not merge the people.
